items.title: A morphism of groupoids bijective on orbits and on isotropy groups is an equivalence
items.author: Massimiliano Puglisi; Thomas Schick; Vito Felice Zenobi
items.work: Stolz Positive Scalar Curvature Structure Groups, Proper Actions and Equivariant 2-Types

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a morphism of groupoids to be an equivalence: it is enough that the morphism induces a bijection between the orbit sets and, for every object, an isomorphism between the isotropy groups (statement lines 1261-1266). The proof is carried by an explicit commutative diagram that writes each groupoid as the disjoint union of the isotropy groups of representatives of its orbits; because the orbits correspond bijectively, the morphism becomes a disjoint union of isomorphisms of the summands, and a disjoint union of equivalences is an equivalence (proof lines 1267-1278). The substance is the decomposition: the diagram is what turns the two hypotheses into a summand-by-summand statement, and the remaining input is the standard closure of equivalences under disjoint unions. The proof is short but complete and contains no forward reference or omission. H2.
